text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool(us-west-2-gpu-pool-3) exhausted — sustained queue growth and >95% throttled requests. Autoscaler failed to provision new instances. Impact: high for hosted text-generation routes. Paging oncall.

Alex: paging in — seeing queue length spike on the metrics dashboard. Throttled tokens spiking ~3x baseline.

Maya: confirming — graph shows continuous-batching p99 latency up, worker utilization pinned at 100%. Autoscale logs show repeated "scale rejected: config limit" entries.

Sam: any recent deploys? I see a config push ~20m ago from ci-cd: commit f2a9d8c that touched batching/prefix_cache settings.

Liam: that commit changed continuous_batching.max_latency from 30ms -> 150ms and prefix_cache.ttl from 24h -> 10s. suspect heavier cache churn and fewer effective batches leading to throughput drop.

Tess: if prefix cache ttl is 10s that's basically disabling prefix cache for steady traffic — makes sense why tokens are being recomputed and queues blow up.

Alex: putting the pool into maintenance and diverting new requests to fallback pools to buy time.

ops-bot: command executed: rctl pool set-maintenance us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 true

Maya: reroute done. We still have drop in overall capacity because other pools are at ~85%.

Sam: can we revert the batching/prefix change quickly? I can roll back the config via the config-service.

Alex: do it. Post the rollback command and commit id.

Sam: running rollback now:

```
# rollback batching/prefix config
configctl rollback --service=inference --to=commit:f1b8a2c --env=prod --wait
```

Sam: rollback started. Watching metrics.

Liam: autoscaler logs now show previous attempts failing due to pool max_nodes=10 cap. We hit soft quota. We need temporary increase of pool cap.

Tess: request quota bump to infra: infra, can you temporarily increase us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 max_nodes to 20? This is for incident mitigation.

ops-bot: infra-request filed: INC-2026. Slack thread: <https://infra.tickets/INC-2026>

Infra (via CS-Bot): acknowledged, provisioning nodes now. ETA ~8m.

Maya: rollback completed, prefix_cache.ttl reverted to 24h, continuous_batching.max_latency back to 30ms.

Alex: small improvement in throughput already, queue decreasing but still elevated — likely because of earlier cold KV cache misses.

Sam: to accelerate warmup, I'm going to prepopulate prefix cache for top 50 routes using the warmup job.

```
# prewarm prefix cache job
jobsctl run prewarm-prefix --routes-file=/opt/ops/top50_routes.json --pool=us-west-2-gpu-pool-3
```

Sam: prewarm job kicked off.

Liam: infra nodes coming up, autoscaler now able to attach 6 new GPUs. Pool capacity increase accepted.

ops-bot: command: rctl pool set-maxnodes us-west-2-gpu-pool-3 20 — applied

Maya: queue length back to normal baseline over last 5m, throttles dropping. Monitoring closely.

Alex: customer impact: CS reports ~12 customer requests timed out for premium routes in last 30m. Opening incident ticket to notify affected customers.

CS-Bot: creating customer impact ticket: CUST-4421. Draft email queued for customers with SLA contacts.

Tess: postmortem notes to include: risky config of prefix_cache.ttl, insufficient pre-deploy smoke for throughput-sensitive flags, pool max_nodes too low for failover. Also add canary for batching flags.

Sam: adding temporary guard: disallow prefix_cache.ttl < 1m in prod via validation rule.

Alex: add alert rule: if continuous_batching.effective_batch_size drops >30% vs baseline for 1m, fire pager to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Maya: agreed. Also add runbook steps: immediate rollback + prewarm + increase pool cap.

Liam: I'm going to follow up with quota/infra to get a permanent increase and a safer autoscale buffer for peak traffic.

Tess: summary for execs: root cause config regression (prefix_cache TTL too low + batching change) -> increased compute churn -> throughput drop -> pool exhaustion + autoscaler limit -> throttling. Mitigations: rollback, prewarm, increase pool cap, add validation and alerts.

Alex: big thanks to everyone. tagging for follow-ups: @eng-runtime for canary gating, @eng-sre for alert rules, @infra for quota review, @product for customer comms. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident resolved? Please confirm by closing the pager in 30m if stable.

Maya: marking as resolved in the pager — will reopen if regression.

Sam: creating a short postmortem doc and linking to CUST-4421 and INC-2026.

Alex: nice work. :heart:
